hints: Rearrange $2x + 5y = 10$ into slope-intercept form $y = mx + c$ by isolating $y$.
Subtract $2x$ and divide by $5$: $y = -\dfrac{2}{5}x + 2$, giving gradient $m_1 = -\dfrac{2}{5}$.
Apply the perpendicular condition $m_1 m_2 = -1$ to obtain $m_2 = -\dfrac{1}{-2/5} = \dfrac{5}{2}$.
walkthrough:
Perpendicular finite gradients multiply to minus one.
Rearrange $2x + 5y = 10$ into slope-intercept form $y = mx + c$:
$$5y = -2x + 10 \implies y = -\dfrac{2}{5}x + 2$$
$$m_1 = -\dfrac{2}{5}$$
